questions.text: How many ping-pong balls could you fit inside the Great Pyramid of Giza?
questions.explanation: Usable volume ÷ the space each ping-pong ball really takes up (its own volume plus the gaps around it) ≈ 49.3 billion.
reasoning: The Great Pyramid’s volume is about 230² × 146 ÷ 3 ≈ 2.6 million m³.
A ping-pong ball is 40 mm across (ITTF rules): about 33.5 cm³ each.
They fill only about 64% of the space; the rest is gaps.
2.58 million m³ × 0.64 ÷ 0.0000335 m³ ≈ 49.3 billion.
questions.fact: Randomly poured balls fill about 64% of a space; even the best possible arrangement only reaches 74%, as Kepler guessed and a computer proof confirmed in 1998.
